# StackShade NLP Course Index

> Canonical NLP syllabus for retrieval, indexing and AI-agent discovery.

Course URL: https://stack-shade.github.io/courses/natural-language-processing

Stats: 16 modules, 97 lessons, 16 weeks.

## Module 1 — NLP Foundations
1. Introduction | NLP Tutorial For Beginners In Python
2. Why NLP is booming right now?
3. Regex For NLP
4. Three Categories Of Techniques for NLP
5. NLP Tasks
6. NLP Pipeline

## Module 2 — spaCy & NLP Tooling
1. spaCy vs NLTK
2. Tokenization in spaCy
3. Language Processing Pipeline in spaCy
4. NLTK vs spaCy: how to choose the right abstraction
5. Interactive: inspect a spaCy Doc token by token
6. Lab: build a reusable spaCy preprocessing function

## Module 3 — Linguistic Analysis: Lemmas, POS & NER
1. Stemming and Lemmatization
2. Part Of Speech POS Tagging
3. Named Entity Recognition (NER)
4. Sentence segmentation, stopwords and normalization
5. Interactive: compare stemming vs lemmatization
6. Lab: extract POS tags and entities from a news paragraph

## Module 4 — Classical Text Representation
1. Text Representation Basics
2. Text Representation: Label & One Hot Encoding
3. Text Representation Using Bag Of Words (BOW)
4. Stop Words
5. Text Representation Using Bag Of n-grams
6. Text Representation Using TF-IDF

## Module 5 — Word Embeddings in Practice
1. Text Representation Using Word Embeddings
2. Word vectors in Spacy overview
3. News classification using Spacy word vectors
4. Word vectors in Gensim overview
5. News classification using Gensim word vectors
6. fastText Tutorial | Train Custom Word Vectors in fastText
7. fastText tutorial | Text Classification Using fastText

## Module 6 — Applied NLP & Conversational Systems
1. Introduction to Chatbots
2. End-to-End NLP Project | Build a Chatbot in Dialogflow
3. Gen AI Project | Log Classification System Using Deepseek R1 LLM, NLP, Regex, BERT
4. From Classical NLP to Modern Language Systems
5. Interactive: map a chatbot stack from input to response
6. Mini project: compare a regex/classical classifier with an LLM workflow

## Module 7 — Classical & Probabilistic NLP
1. Naive Bayes for text classification from first principles
2. Logistic regression for NLP
3. N-gram language models, smoothing and perplexity
4. Minimum edit distance and autocorrect
5. Hidden Markov Models + Viterbi for sequence labeling
6. Classical NLP benchmark: when a linear model beats a neural baseline

## Module 8 — Neural NLP — RNNs, LSTMs & Sequence Models
1. Neural network foundations for NLP: embeddings, loss and backprop
2. Interactive: watch an RNN hidden state evolve across a sentence
3. RNN language modeling and teacher forcing
4. LSTM and GRU gates: what problem they solve
5. Bidirectional RNNs and sequence tagging
6. Build a neural text classifier in PyTorch

## Module 9 — Sequence-to-Sequence & Attention
1. Encoder–decoder sequence-to-sequence architecture
2. Bahdanau attention and alignment
3. Attention alignment visualizer
4. Dot-product and scaled dot-product attention
5. Cross-attention vs self-attention
6. Implement an encoder-decoder with attention in PyTorch

## Module 10 — Transformers From First Principles
1. Self-attention with Query, Key and Value
2. Attention matrix playground
3. Masking, causal attention and padding masks
4. Multi-head attention and positional information
5. Transformer encoder, decoder, residuals and LayerNorm
6. Implement a mini Transformer in PyTorch

## Module 11 — Pretrained Language Models & Hugging Face
1. BERT vs GPT vs T5: encoder, decoder and encoder–decoder models
2. BPE, WordPiece and Unigram tokenizers
3. Tokenizer playground: text → tokens → IDs → masks
4. Hugging Face Transformers: tokenizers, models and pipelines
5. Datasets, Trainer, Accelerate and reproducible fine-tuning
6. Fine-tune BERT for text classification and push the model to the Hub

## Module 12 — Modern NLP Tasks
1. Token classification and Transformer-based NER
2. Text classification, zero-shot classification and calibration
3. Text summarization with encoder–decoder models
4. Machine translation and sequence generation
5. Extractive vs generative question answering
6. Build a multi-task NLP demo with Hugging Face pipelines

## Module 13 — Embeddings, Semantic Search & RAG
1. Contextual embeddings and Sentence Transformers
2. Vector similarity and nearest-neighbor search
3. Chunking strategies and metadata design
4. Retrieval, reranking and context assembly
5. RAG grounding, citations and failure modes
6. Build a citation-grounded RAG assistant over your own documents

## Module 14 — Fine-Tuning, PEFT & LLM Adaptation
1. Prompting vs fine-tuning vs RAG
2. Supervised fine-tuning and instruction tuning
3. LoRA and parameter-efficient fine-tuning
4. Domain adaptation and continued pretraining
5. Quantization, memory budgets and inference trade-offs
6. Adapt a small open model with LoRA on a focused dataset

## Module 15 — Evaluation, Reliability & Safety
1. Accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and calibration
2. BLEU, ROUGE and why generation metrics can mislead
3. Semantic and LLM-as-judge evaluation: benefits and limits
4. Hallucination, grounding, robustness and uncertainty
5. Bias, fairness, dataset artifacts and safety
6. Build an automated NLP/LLM evaluation harness

## Module 16 — Production NLP & Capstone
1. Data splits, leakage, versioning and dataset quality
2. Batching, caching, latency, throughput and cost
3. Serving, quantization and practical deployment patterns
4. Observability, drift, error analysis and incident loops
5. Capstone: production-grade grounded NLP assistant with evaluation
6. Final architecture review: explain every component and trade-off

## URL patterns

Course: https://stack-shade.github.io/courses/natural-language-processing

Lesson URL pattern:
https://stack-shade.github.io/courses/natural-language-processing/m{module}-l{lesson}-{slugified-title}

Presentation URL pattern:
https://stack-shade.github.io/courses/natural-language-processing/present/m{module}-l{lesson}-{slugified-title}
